pr_title: Search - add search box control and implement search experience
pr_body:
<!-- Enter a brief description/summary of your PR here. What does it fix/what does it change/how was it tested (even manually, if necessary)? -->
This is the PR for feature Search: #605 
This PR includes the newly introduced SearchBoxControl in TermControl dir, which is the search bar for the search experience. And the codes that enable Search in Windows Terminal. 

<!-- Other than the issue solved, is this relevant to any other issues/existing PRs? --> 
The PR that migrates the Conhost search module: https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/pull/3279
Spec (still actively updating): https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/pull/3299
<!-- Please review the items on the PR checklist before submitting-->
## PR Checklist
* [x] Closes #605 
* [ ] CLA signed. If not, go over [here](https://cla.opensource.microsoft.com/microsoft/Terminal) and sign the CLA
* [ ] Tests added/passed
* [ ] Requires documentation to be updated
* [ ] I've discussed this with core contributors already. If not checked, I'm ready to accept this work might be rejected in favor of a different grand plan. Issue number where discussion took place: #xxx

<!-- Provide a more detailed description of the PR, other things fixed or any additional comments/features here -->
These functionalities are included in the search experience. 
1. Search in Terminal text buffer. 
2. Automatic wrap-around. 
3. Search up or down switch by clicking different buttons.
4. Search case sensitively/insensitively by clicking a button.                                                                                                                                                S. Move the search box to the top/bottom by clicking a button. 
6. Close by clicking 'X'. 
7. Open search by ctrl + F.

When the searchbox is open, the user could still interact with the terminal by clicking the terminal input area. 

While I already have the search functionalities, currently there are still some known to-do works and I will keep updating my PR:

1. Optimize the search box UI, this includes:
                                                  1) Theme adaptation. The search box background and font color 
                                                       should change according to the theme, 
                                                  2) Add background. Currently the elements in search box are all
                                                      transparent. However, we need a background. 
                                                  3) Move button should be highlighted once clicked. 
2. Accessibility: search process should be able to performed without mouse. Once the search box is focused, the user should be able to navigate between all interactive elements on the searchbox using keyboard. 

<!-- Describe how you validated the behavior. Add automated tests wherever possible, but list manual validation steps taken as well -->

To test:
1. checkout this branch.
2. Build the project. 
3. Start Windows Terminal and press Ctrl+F
4. The search box should appear on the top right corner.

issue_context.title: Feature Request: Search
issue_context.body:
One of the superior features of iTerm2 (sadly only available on macOS) is it's content search.  The search comes in two variants: search from active tab and search from all tabs. For those unfamiliar with iTerm2 and wondering, this feature would roughly equate to almost any editor like Visual Studio Code string search.

I haven't gone in-depth with the output buffering in Terminal yet to validate if this feature is realistically doable at the current state of the Terminal app, but this is a usability feature for multitasking terminal users that would be worth a LOT.
comments: I'll repurpose this as our main Search epic issue. I'm glad the community seems to have figured out our backlog and I don't need to go add it myself. :smile:

That would be pretty great 👀 
With regex support ? 😸

Another thing to keep in consideration about how iTerm2 works, is you can "Ctrl+f" to search, then press Tab when you find what you want, and it will copy what you searched for.  Basically you can easily find something in the output and copy/paste it to the input without ever leaving your keyboard.

It will be great if the search history can be traversed with `Arrow up` and `Arrow down` key.

BTW just a suggestion. 😸
(for the record, I believe #3279 was the first step on the path to this feature landing, but it's not quite finished yet. Thanks though msftbot)
Amazing! Can we expect a new search feature in the next release?

@kell18 While this feature is in active development currently, I _personally_ don't think it's going to make it quite in time for the next release cut unfortunately. Ideally, it _should_ land in the December release (which is why this is marked for the "1912" milestone), but I'm making no commitments 😝

review_comments: should the search box be in control of its own `Escape` key handler?

is this because we are using PreviewKeyDown? I finally understand why we needed to check `ContainsFocus`

Yes, this can fully separate the Search Dialog and the Terminal
(as I mention below: I think this can be handled in `SearchBoxControl`'s `TextBox::KeyDown`, so long as the event is marked `Handled(true)`)
You'll probably want to mark the event as handled here too, at least for Enter and Escape

Would it be better to just set the `SearchBoxControl`'s `Visibility` to `Collapsed` when it's closed, and then back to `Visible` when it's re-opened, as opposed to destroying it and re-creating it each time?
I would just destroy it, people won't close and re-create the search dialog very frequently and I think it is dangerous to always have a dialog hidden there.

The original comment got lost, here it is from another thread:
> Can this ever be hit? Doesn't all input go to the SearchBox by nature of it having focus?

> Yes, it will and I think it is important. Terminal control uses a tunneling strategy on key input. Any input (including inputs on the search box because it is a child of TermControl) will be received by TermControl first and handled in this _KeyDownHandler. Thus, I added this check to separate inputs on TermControl and search box, this avoids lots of werid bugs. 

> That sounds like a bug to me - I think if the `SearchBoxControl` marks the `KeyDown` event as `Handled(true)`, then it shouldn't bubble up to the `TermControl`

I still don't think this should be necessary, and that `SearchBoxControl` should be able to handle this without letting it bubble up
I think I need to try if we can handle within SearchBoxControl, I will not take this as a blocker.
I resolve this for now and I will add this in my follow issue: https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/issues/3942
Feature request:  I think the SearchBox should listen for the Esc key to close search.
Added. But through making Searchbox listening to KeyDown events, not key bindings
If the user clicks in the terminal control while the searchbox is up, does focus move back to the TermControl?  If it does, should the else block here call _searchBox.SetFocusOnTextbox();?
Yes, the focus will move back to TermControl. Moved SetFocusOnTextbox out of the if check.
Is this still true when you are in the scrollback?

I think so. mutableViewport moves with the written text so the end of this view port is also the end of the text. If we scroll back, we change another member _scrollOffset. You can see on line 379 of Terminal.cpp, the visible end index need to substract _scrollOffset
Why was the conditional surrounding this line removed?

With the surrounding condition, the search module cannot support single letter search. However, because that FindNext() only returns true if there is a match, as long as we check before we select, there should be a text match (including a single letter. )
Ah okay. It's a [`_coordSelStart`, `_coordSelEnd`] selection, not a [`_coordSelStart`, `_coordSelEnd`) - that makes more sense then.
these should be in a `private:` section.
It strikes me as odd that the ViewStartIndex has no _, implying public. But the matching ViewEndIndex is still prefixed with _, implying private. Do you not need both?
changed _ViewEndIndex to public and removed the "_"

Tested with a Terminal guy using Accessibility Insights, and it could successfully find the selection.
